summary: Layout-aware scientific PDF structure parser (stdlib + poppler-utils only): extracts title, abstract, authors/affiliations, numbered sections with hierarchy, paragraphs, tables (Markdown+rows), figures, display equations, references, repeated headers/footers, and clean per-page plaintext — every element with page+bbox evidence. benchmark.py provides a runnable A/B against a bare raw-text read.

method.parse: pdftohtml -xml (line-level font/bbox) + pdftotext -layout; column detection, reading-order grouping, section/hierarchy recognition, table/equation/reference extraction.
method.front_matter: authors + affiliations from the page-1 author block; repeated header/footer text from page margins.
method.evidence: every section/paragraph/table/figure/equation/reference carries page + bbox; plaintext_pages keeps inline numbers intact.
method.benchmark: benchmark.py compares a bare raw-text read (0 structured elements) vs the parser (sections+tables+figures+equations+references with 1.0 evidence coverage).

self_test.input: public sample arXiv:1706.03762 (Attention Is All You Need, 15 pages, 2-column)
self_test.result: parsed 15 pages; sections incl. Background/Model Architecture/Results/Conclusion with hierarchy; figures/tables/captions located with bboxes; references extracted; full text 36KB
self_test.notes: self-test uses a public paper, not the hidden fixed cases; the platform supplies actual cases at evaluation time.

deviations_from_paper: Vector/path-only figures are recorded as image regions by bbox but their interior content is not rasterized into text (out of scope).
Rotation and non-Latin CJK glyph shaping depend on poppler output and are flagged when uncertain.

failure_modes.handling: fall back to pdftotext; if that fails, report uncertainty and return partial structure

failure_modes.case: scanned/image PDF with no text layer
failure_modes.handling: report 'no text layer' in uncertainty; do not fabricate text
global fontspec map keyed by font id

expected_outputs.note: text-form self-test example on a public paper (marked as example)
